question: What is the sex ratio of India as per 2011 census?
solution:
The correct answer is __**943 females per 1000 males**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sex Ratio:

 
 
• In the Population Census of 2011, it was revealed that the population ratio in India in 2011 is 943 females per 1000 males.
 
• The sex ratio is used to describe the number of females per 1000 males.
 
• Sex ratio is a valuable source for finding the population of women in India and what is the ratio of women to that of men in India.
 
• The Sex Ratio 2011 shows an upward trend from the census 2001 data.
 
• Census 2001 revealed that there were 933 females to that of 1000 males.
 
• For decades India has seen a decrease in the sex ratio, but since the last two decades, there has been a slight increase in the sex ratio.
 
• Over the last five decades, the sex ratio has been moving from around 930 females to that of 1000 males.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Kerala - 1084
 
• Puducherry - 1037
 
• Tamil Nadu - 996
 
• Andhra Pradesh - 993
 
• Chhattisgarh - 991
 
• Andaman and Nicobar Island - 876
 
• Delhi - 868
 
• Chandigarh - 818
 
• Dadra and Nagar Haveli - 774
